newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Press reports yesterday said late PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou had designated his wife, Dimitra Liani, life-time president of a foundation to be established in his name. The news is expected to set fur flying once again in the party, where there are efforts under way to wrest control of Papandreou's archives from Liani.

--The Turkish expert committe on relations with Greece is reported to have urged the beginning of direct talks between Athens and Ankara on differences in the Aegean in its memorandum to the Dutch EU presidency.

--There are reports that the government is considering including up to 250,000 illegally constructed buildings in town planning zones to boost revenues, regardless of the environmental cost. The majority of the buildings are constructed on state forest land.

--Greece will celebrate this year's World Environment Day with mountains of rubbish on city streets as rubbish collectors continue their protests for the second day and locals continue to protest plans to create land-fills in suburban areas.
--The government appears unlikely to honour a recent Supreme Court decision allowing both parents to receive family benefits.

--The appointment of Richard Holbrooke as new US presidential emissary to Cyprus is considered to be an indication of the urgency the Clinton administration places on a resolution of the Cyprus problem. Holbrooke brokered a Bosnia peace agreement and also mediated in the stand-off between Greece and Turkey over Imia last year.
--The government is reportedly considering the establishment of private sector technical colleges, following a plethora of voices calling for private tertiary education.
--Some 150,000 illegal buildings will revert to the state in an effort to extract outstanding debts estimated at 250 billion drachmas.
